new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-phonemic and computed from the right edge of the word by counting vowels (moras, since /VV/ counts as two /V/): in a vowel-final word the syllable containing the penultimate /V/ is stressed (penult for CV-syllable words, but a final CVV syllable takes the stress), in a consonant-final word the last syllable is stressed; going leftward, the syllable containing every second /V/ before a stressed one is also stressed (a moraic right-to-left alternating pattern). Under narrow conditions (107c: three preceding light syllables, vowel identity, cluster conditions) a three-syllable stress unit occurs, but never at the end of the word. §101 (p. 19): 'there is a systematic stress pattern and a very elaborate intonational apparatus, although no stress phonemes nor phonemic pitch levels are necessary to describe the prosody'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Four degrees (§107d, p. 26): strong stress on the last stressed syllable before the juncture /./ (unless the suprasegmental phoneme /'/ of §161 occurs earlier); intermediate stress on every other syllable selected by 107a,c (i.e. the leftward alternating stresses); weak stress on an initial syllable that is not otherwise stressed (107b); all others unstressed. Stress units (§107e) of 1-3 syllables tend to equal duration (stress-timed rhythm, p. 27).
new_statements.exceptions: 107c: a three-syllable stress unit (stress on the third syllable before a stressed one) only when the three preceding syllables each contain a single /V/, the second-preceding vowel is identical to an adjoining vowel, and specified consonant-cluster conditions hold; examples /,suwah,kwinunu'hihti./ 'is dizzy'. No stress ever on the third syllable from the end with the intervening syllables unstressed. Suprasegmental phoneme /'/ (§161) can shift the strong stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonemic word (bounded by the word-juncture /+/); the description is of the Northfork subdialect (North Fork, Madera County) of Western Mono, based on one main speaker (Lucy Kinsman) from 1953-55 fieldwork; stress marked in examples though not phonemic. Sentence-level strong stress is defined relative to the juncture /./.
new_statements.identity_note: Lamb 1958 describes 'Northfork Mono', the Northfork subdialect of the San Joaquin (Western Mono) dialect, from North Fork, Madera County (intro pp. 15-16 and preface). Glottolog 5.x mono1275 is language-level with no dialect children, so no separate glottocode exists for Western vs. Eastern Mono (Owens Valley Paiute); the Eastern dialect is not covered by this statement (Norris 1986 would be the source).

sources.note: §101 p.19: systematic stress pattern, 'no stress phonemes nor phonemic pitch levels are necessary'; §107 pp.24-26: stress automatic, counted from the right edge — V-final words stress the syllable containing the next-to-last /V/, C-final words the last syllable; every second /V/ leftward also stressed; initial syllable otherwise weak; four degrees of stress; three-syllable stress units under conditions 107c.
